label: T2.7-green - the place the PROJECT builds boots, wires and reads as the game the spec describes. Re-run after the previous pass's two open findings (no Lighting configured at all; a player spawning 917 studs from their own dome) were fixed at the root, along with four defects this run's own measurements found. Multi-client contention, cross-server persistence and real input remain UNTESTABLE here.

provenance.note: Compared the rojo read API's flattened tree against the DataModel by dmPath and source length, BOTH directions. The place also had three pre-existing mounts from an earlier sync (Server_PRE_EXISTING, Shared_PRE_EXISTING, Client_PRE_EXISTING); renaming a Script does not stop it running, so ServerScriptService.Server_PRE_EXISTING was booting the game a SECOND time - which is why 60 plots produced 120 domes on the first attempt. All three were parked into ServerStorage before this run.

phases.name: sync-provenance
phases.detail: 48 scripts, 0 mismatches in either direction. FALSIFIED FIRST: renaming ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Layout drove mismatchCount 0 -> 2, reporting BOTH halves (MISSING ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Layout and UNDECLARED ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Layout_FALSIFY); the rename was then inverted and the count returned to 0. A one-sided check would pass a place carrying extra scripts.

phases.name: boot-console
phases.detail: NEGATIVE: zero engine errors across boot with the new WorldService in the registry. Warnings are the 14 expected per-action B2-security notices plus the monetization-unconfigured notice (7 inert catalog entries at asset id 0 - a human handoff item, not a defect). POSITIVE: the discovered marker '[JoinRetry]' MUST appear and did, 8 times - plot.fetch, salvage.fetch, daily.claim, structures.fetch, leaderboard.fetch, depth.fetch, offline.peek, resurface.fetch each re-issued after the data push. A silent console there would be indistinguishable from a missing guard.

phases.name: server-authority
phases.detail: capture-S / act / capture-S' over the REAL wire. structures.fetch quoted nextCost 303 with drones at Lv6 and salvage.fetch reporting rate 3.50; after structures.buy{key='drones'}: Credits 419 -> 116 (spent exactly 303, the server-derived price - MATCH true), drones 6 -> 7, and the rate REPORTED BY salvage.fetch 3.50 -> 4.00. The delta is read from a DIFFERENT service than the one that acted, which is the written-never-read discipline. Stronger than the previous run: the catalog's own effect block PREDICTED current=3.50 next=4.00 delta=0.50 before the purchase, and the observed delta matched it to within 1e-9. Two earlier attempts failed on guessed field names (`credits`, `cost`); the shape was then read once and reported rather than guessed a third time.

phases.name: client-wire
phases.detail: All 14 actions in Net.Actions invoked through ReplicatedStorage.CoreGateway FROM THE CLIENT DATAMODEL - the only rung that crosses the replication boundary. Set-diff clean: 14 declared, 14 exercised. ZERO RateLimited, ZERO UnknownAction, ZERO throws (any of the three means the request never reached its handler, i.e. unverified rather than verified-and-refused). Replies: plot.fetch/salvage.fetch/salvage.collect/structures.fetch/structures.buy/depth.fetch/offline.peek/offline.claim/resurface.fetch/leaderboard.fetch = ok; plot.claim = AlreadyClaimed; daily.claim = OnCooldown; depth.descend and resurface.do = PrereqUnmet. Every refusal is the handler's own documented gate, never Internal.

phases.name: world-present
phases.detail: THE PLACE WAS EMPTIED FIRST, which is what makes this number mean anything: the previous pass reported 658 Workspace descendants and 'the single SpawnLocation is at (0, 0.5, 0)' and read as healthy, but every one of those belonged to the Studio place the tree had been synced into. `grep -c SpawnLocation` on the built .rbxlx was 0, as was Baseplate, as was every Lighting property. Workspace was reduced to 0 non-character BaseParts before boot; everything below was built by the game. 285 BaseParts, bounds 1152 x 931 x 1152. 60 dome models with 0 duplicate names, radii 160..496 (was a single ring at 917). Trench1 floor span 1248, half-span 624 against an outermost pad edge of 528 - COVERED with 96 studs of margin, and under Roblox's 2048-stud Part ceiling. Rim: a Folder of 24 tangent segments at radius 576, longest edge 153 studs. Exactly 1 SpawnLocation, the game's own DeepReachArrival.ArrivalPad. Zero Neon parts wider than 200 studs. The player stands at (160, 2.5, 0), 3 studs from dome_1's pad and 160 from the arrival pad, Running with velocity 0.00 and dome_1.Shell.Pad under them on a CanCollide-respecting raycast.

phases.name: screens
phases.detail: Three shots, each assertion stated BEFORE the capture. Two pass, one cannot-tell. No assertion failed. The cannot-tell is recorded as an open finding rather than laundered into a pass.

screens.assertion: At the player's own eye height the scene reads as deep water - dark, cold-tinted, bounded by fog, with bioluminescent accents - and NOT as an outdoor daylight scene; and no single element floods the frame.
screens.detail: Dark blue water, visible fog wall, dome silhouettes at distance, drifting motes, the player's glass shell overhead and the trench floor underfoot. This is the assertion the PREVIOUS run failed: the place had no Lighting configured at all and opened on a bright blue afternoon sky. The 'no single element floods the frame' half was added because two separate elements did during this run and both were fixed - see findings rim-is-a-disc and pad-is-a-floodlight.

screens.assertion: The game builds its own arrival platform at the ring centre: a lit SpawnLocation with solid ground under it, distinct from any Studio place furniture.
screens.detail: The pad is visible as a lit platform at the origin with its PointLight casting onto the trench floor, and the in-world leaderboard sign ('TOP DIVERS - LIFETIME CREDITS') is legible beyond it. Captured after Workspace was emptied of the place's own Baseplate and SpawnLocation, so nothing in frame is inherited.

screens.assertion: From a camera pulled back to ~190 studs the dome ring and trench floor remain visible rather than black, so a player who zooms out can still navigate.
screens.detail: The picture shows dome silhouettes and several pad PointLights as navigational anchors against a very dark field - it is not black, but it is dim. What the picture CANNOT settle is whether dim is wrong: the spec asks for 'quiet, high-pressure, industrial-deep-sea', and how dark that should be at zoom is a taste judgement a human playtest makes, not one a screenshot makes. Lighting was already lifted once during this run against exactly this shot (Brightness 1 -> 1.4, Ambient rgb(12,26,38) -> rgb(20,42,56), EnvironmentDiffuseScale 0.35 -> 0.5), which improved it without costing the eye-level read. Filed as finding scene-dark-at-zoom with the knobs named.

findings.summary: The scene is dim when the camera is pulled well back, and pulling the camera back is the first thing a tycoon player does.
findings.measured: At a 190-stud overhead camera the domes read as faint silhouettes; the legible anchors are the pad PointLights. At the player's own eye height the scene reads correctly. Ambient - not Brightness - is the load-bearing knob: Brightness lights the faces the sun reaches, which on a field of glass domes seen from above is almost nothing.
findings.why: A deliberate trade against the spec's 'quiet, high-pressure' theme. FogEnd 420 also means the far side of a 1152-stud world is never visible from the near side, which is a real tension with the spec's 'progression is legible from across the map'.
findings.knobs: WorldService.LIGHTING_NUMBERS.Brightness (1.4), .EnvironmentDiffuseScale (0.5), .FogEnd (420); WorldService.LIGHTING_COLORS.Ambient / .OutdoorAmbient. world.spec holds Brightness <= 1.5 and FogEnd <= 600, so there is headroom inside the guards.
findings.owner: human (T3) - a taste judgement, not a defect

findings.summary: HUD slot content still truncates below ~820px of viewport height; the panels no longer overlap, but content is clipped away.
findings.measured: Carried forward from the previous pass and unchanged by this one. Every capture in this session was at 1600x670, where the STRUCTURES panel's last row and the DEPTH readout are cut off. The overlap was fixed by ClipsDescendants; making the catalog SCROLL is the outstanding follow-up.

findings.summary: All 7 monetization catalog entries carry asset id 0 and are therefore inert.
findings.measured: The game warns loudly at boot, by name, for all 7. No gamepass can be granted and no receipt recognised, so the purchase analytics event has no reachable emit point.
findings.owner: human - the ids can only be created on the published place

fixedThisRun: no-spawn-in-built-place: `rojo build` produced a place with an empty Workspace - 0 SpawnLocation, 0 Baseplate, 0 Lighting properties. Published as-is a joiner would materialise at the origin with no floor and fall forever. WorldService now owns the scene and the game's one SpawnLocation.
no-lighting-configured: the spec's 'Theme & tone' section had no code behind it because nothing owned the scene. The reachability gate had been emitting this as a non-blocking WARN the whole time.

floor-misses-the-ring: DepthService sized the trench floor from a private SHELL_SPAN_STUDS = 640, commented as covering a 12-dome server. The registry is Players.MaxPlayers, so a 60-seat server left every dome 629 studs past the floor's edge - measured in-engine at 917 vs 320 before the fix. No Part may exceed 2048 studs, so no slab could ever have covered the old ring at its 3056-stud ceiling. Fixed by bounding the layout (concentric rings, O(sqrt n)) and deriving the floor from it in shared/Layout.
spawn-917-studs-from-your-own-dome: PlotService.seatFor now places the player on their own pad on claim and on every respawn, reading the tier from the persisted blob.

rim-is-a-disc: the tier boundary was one Part with Shape = Cylinder - a SOLID DISC of radius 576, Neon, on all six tiers, lying over the entire trench with every player underneath one. It covered the bottom 40% of the frame. Now 24 tangent segments.
pad-is-a-floodlight: Neon is fullbright, so a lit pad at rgb(64,226,255) across a 64-stud deck was a light source rather than a lit surface. Now rgb(18,70,92).
duplicate-domes-on-a-saved-place: buildDome now ADOPTS an existing dome by name the way buildShell already did; a place saved with a built world otherwise boots into a stacked duplicate set.
unverified: Multi-client contention: one Studio client only. Two players racing for the last free dome is UNTESTABLE here.
Cross-server persistence: a single server. Session-lock stealing and cross-server exclusion need two real servers.
Real player input: every action was invoked through the gateway, not driven by a human pressing keys. Controls, camera feel and prompt reachability are unverified.
Performance: no frame-time or memory measurement was taken, at any player count.
Long-horizon economy: offline accrual was exercised over seconds, not over the hours the balance is tuned for.

The depth axis as a VISUAL: tier floors are solid, so a deeper dome is not actually visible from a shallower one. Whether the spec's 'legible from across the map' is satisfied is unresolved and was not asserted here.
